card.name: Adjectives before the word language
card.fires_on: Describing adjectives that sit right before a word like language, words, terms or questions, after verbs like use or write. Typical examples are loaded, simple, offensive, technical and similar.

modes.label: Style adjective after use
modes.description: An adjective describing the kind of wording, right after a verb like use or include.
modes.example: Tim O'Brien uses<< simple>> words and phrases to great effect.

modes.label: Adjective in a negated or listed phrase
modes.description: A tone adjective in a phrase about what wording is allowed or avoided.
modes.example: although cursing and<< offensive>> language are not.

modes.label: Part of a compound modifier
modes.description: A word inside a hyphenated or compound modifier that leads to terms or language.
modes.example: We use non-<<technical>> language, to make field identifications easier

card.writes: It pushes the next word toward language and Language, in English and Chinese.
card.plain: It fires on a describing word when the next word is likely to be language, as in simple or offensive language.
